Reduce the aggressive bend so the dominant gesture stays calm while the new void/threshold becomes legible.
Add a small access seam at the frontage side to create a clearer public threshold without destroying the primary mass.
Align the notch with the program-frame access side so the ground response matches the verified road frontage in the diagram.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent four-view mass and the dominant object remains readable, but it behaves mostly as a compact extruded block with a mild bent/tilted top rather than a neighborhood-building with an active ground threshold. The blue frontage edge is not answered by a clear public void, undercut, or entry seam; the mass stays sealed at grade and the court logic is too weak to register as usable public space. Silhouette is acceptable and not visibly self-colliding across views, so repair integrity is decent, but program appropriateness fails because the visible section and base-to-street relationship do not support the required neighborhood_living contract. The form also leans closer to a generic prism with minor upper articulation than to a public-facing court/terrace building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Taller mixed-use tower language; its skyline emphasis should not be copied directly into this lower neighborhood-living mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mass can read as a strong civic object when one side is cut into a clear profile/step relation; useful for controlled silhouette and upper hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More cafe/restaurant than broader neighborhood living; the tower/sign element is not a direct massing template.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A calm low horizontal body with a distinct attached vertical marker can support neighborhood use while keeping the ground edge legible.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied from the visible diagram, but the access edge response is semantically weak.
